feature: A copied icon leaves its blank canvas out
summary: Copy Merged (Shift Command C) on a drawing made on a blank canvas now puts only the drawing on the clipboard, with nothing behind it, the same picture Export saves by default. Screenshots and photographs still copy whole.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. The walk is copy-leaves-the-canvas-out-walk.

try.do: File > New, then pick the Pen (P) and draw a closed shape on the white canvas.
Press Escape, then Shift Command C.
Paste into something dark (a dark chat, Keynote on a dark slide, Preview's File > New from Clipboard) and look at the corners.
Open a screenshot and press Shift Command C.
Paste it into the same dark place and check the whole screenshot came with it.

evaluate: Does the pasted icon sit on the dark colour with no white box round it?
Does the pasted screenshot still carry every pixel of its background?
Is it clear enough, without a sheet, that a copy of a drawing on a blank canvas leaves the canvas out?
rough: The copy WITH the canvas (your answer B: hold Option and Copy Merged becomes Copy Merged with Background) is not in the menu yet. Option Shift Command C already belongs to Copy Look, and a Mac menu can only swap a row under Option when both rows share one key, so the white version is on a decision card. Until you answer, Export with Include the background ticked is the way to get it.

Only the whole-picture copy changed. Copy Merged with a marquee up still copies the white inside the marquee, because that copy pastes back into Photonz as a layer where the white is part of what you picked.
The pictures are the app window; the clipboard's own contents were checked by the walk reading the four corners of the copied PNG, not photographed on a dark page.
